newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Stocks, dollar pause before Greenspan speech.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Stocks, dollar pause before Greenspan speech.

text.p: European stock markets and the dollar paused on Tuesday after record-breaking runs as dealers waited to see if U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan would again try to trip up the raging bull on Wall Street.

London and Frankfurt stocks slipped back as apprehension grew over whether Greenspan, who was to testify to the U.S. Senate later in the day, would repeat his warning of irrational exuberance which sent share prices reeling last December.

"The Greenspan speech is the key to what happens today," one London dealer said. "The last time he spoke he said the market was overheated and since then we've had a rise of another 500 points. So he might well try to trip up that gigantic bull across the water."
Wall Street, where the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed up 10.77 points on Monday at a record 6,843.87, seemed to be losing its power to pull European markets up on its coat tails.

By mid-morning on Tuesday London's FTSE index, which has hit a string of Dow-induced records since the New Year, was down 15.5 at 4,178.5. In Frankfurt the DAX slipped below the 3,000 barrier which it breached last week to 2,988.12, down 42.56.
Paris likewise took a breather, with the CAC-40 index down 6.75 at 2,399.35.

But channel tunnel owner Eurotunnel extended Monday's 5.8 percent gain on higher 1996 revenues and prospects for completion of a bank debt accord by March. The share was up 4.79 percent at 7.65 francs ($1.39).
London investors, who bought heavily last week when finance minister Kenneth Clarke left interest rates unchanged, had the extra worry of a renewed central bank call for higher rates.

Bank of England Governor Eddie George, engaged in a tug of war with Clarke who has the final say on monetary policy, warned that there were "real dangers" in letting sterling strength delay an interest rate rise.
His comments rekindled market speculation that interest rates could go up in early February even though Clarke is not keen on the idea before the general election due by May.

"Eddie George seems to be getting a little more strident in his views on interest rates," one trader said. "We will see a bit of selling pushing the market down today -- no wild selling but just a reluctance of institutions to put more into London."
On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar took a breather after hitting an almost four year high against the yen on Monday. Again all eyes were on Greenspan.

"Greenspan's comments today will dominate. I think the consensual view is that the Fed is not going to do anything to tighten monetary policy in February but that there will be tightening further down the road," said NatWest Markets currency strategist Kit Juckes.

The dollar was steady at 1.6230 marks compared with Monday's late European level of 1.6258 with an index from the IFO organisation indicating a soft German business climate having had little influence.
The dollar was also stable at 118.40 yen after breaching the the 118 barrier for the first time in almost four years on Monday.
CURRENCIES AT 1030 GMT
The dollar was trading at 118.40 yen and 1.6230 marks compared with Monday's late European levels of 117.97 and 1.6258.
STOCK MARKETS
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was down 15.5 points at 4,178.5
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was at 2,399.35, down 6.75. The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was down 42.56 at 2,988.12
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened at $353.35, compared with a $353.65 close in London on Monday. Silver was easier at $472 after closing Monday at $4.75. ($1=5.500 French Franc)
